extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent attorneys/representatives, national patent offices, and European Patent Office officials
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules under the Convention on the Grant of European Patents and its Implementing Regulations governing filing, representation, PCT interaction, publication, transfer, fees, language, transitional arrangements and related administrative matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: European patent application as object of property (Article 148)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 74 shall apply unless the group of Contracting States has specified otherwise. The group of Contracting States may provide that a European patent application for which these Contracting States are designated may only be transferred, mortgaged or subjected to any legal means of execution in respect of all the Contracting States of the group and in accordance with the provisions of the special agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits groups of Contracting States to treat designation as indivisible for property-transfer/enforcement purposes and to require transfers/mortgages to cover all group States per a special agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint designation of grouped States (Article 149)
rubrics_metrics.description: The group of Contracting States may provide that these States may only be designated jointly, and that the designation of one or some only of such States shall be deemed to constitute the designation of all the States of the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a group is so provided, designating any one member may be treated as designating all; applies also where the EPO is designated and applicant indicates desire to obtain a European patent for one or more of the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) (Article 150)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Cooperation Treaty shall be applied in accordance with the provisions of this Part. International applications filed under the Cooperation Treaty may be the subject of proceedings before the European Patent Office; in case of conflict, the provisions of the Cooperation Treaty shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT timing and substantive provisions govern international applications before the EPO; specifically, the time limit to file a request for examination under Article 94(2) of the Convention shall not expire before the time prescribed by PCT Articles 22 or 39.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO may act as a receiving Office (Article 151)
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Patent Office may act as a receiving Office within the meaning of the PCT if the applicant is a resident or national of a Contracting State to this Convention in respect of which the PCT has entered into force; may also act if applicant is resident/national of a State not a Contracting State to this Convention but a PCT contracting state with an agreement; and, subject to prior approval of the Administrative Council, may act for any other applicant per agreement with WIPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines eligibility and required agreements for the EPO to receive international (PCT) applications; institutional approvals required for broader reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and transmittal of international applications (Article 152)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant chooses the European Patent Office as a receiving Office, he shall file it directly with the EPO. If filed through the central industrial property office, the Contracting State must ensure timely transmittal so EPO can comply with PCT transmittal conditions. Each international application is subject to payment of the transmittal fee, payable on filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies direct filing route or timely transmittal via national office and the obligation to pay the transmittal fee upon filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO as designated Office and Examining Division competence (Article 153)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall act as a designated Office under the PCT for Contracting States to this Convention for which the PCT has entered into force and which are designated in the international application if the applicant informs the receiving Office he wishes to obtain a European patent for these States. When so acting, the Examining Division is competent to take decisions required under PCT Article 25(2)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets when an international (PCT) application is treated as a European patent application and allocates decision-making competence to the Examining Division for certain PCT-required decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO as International Searching Authority (ISA) (Article 154)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall act as an ISA for applicants who are residents or nationals of a Contracting State in respect of which the PCT has entered into force, subject to an agreement with WIPO. Subject to prior approval of the Administrative Council, it may act as ISA for other applicants per agreement. The Boards of Appeal decide on protests against additional fees charged under PCT Article 17(3)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines conditions and governance for EPO acting as ISA and provides appeal route for fee-related protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO as International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA) (Article 155)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall act as IPEA within the meaning of PCT Chapter II for applicants who are residents or nationals of a Contracting State bound by that Chapter, subject to agreement with WIPO; subject to Administrative Council approval it may act for others per agreement. Boards of Appeal decide on protests against additional fees under PCT Article 34(3)(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous conditions to ISA; administrative approvals and appeal paths for fee protests.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO as elected Office (Article 156)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall act as an elected Office if the applicant has elected any of the designated States for which PCT Chapter II has become binding. Subject to prior approval, the same applies where the applicant is resident or national of a non-party State if the Assembly of the International Patent Cooperation Union has decided to allow that person to make a demand for international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets when EPO acts as elected Office under PCT Chapter II and the exceptional cases dependent on Assembly or Administrative Council permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: International search report replaces European search report; supplementary European search (Article 157)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report under PCT Article 18 or any declaration under PCT Article 17(2)(a), and their publication under PCT Article 21, shall take the place of the European search report and the mention of its publication in the European Patent Bulletin. Subject to Administrative Council decisions, a supplementary European search report shall be drawn up in respect of all international applications; the applicant shall pay the search fee at same time as the national fee provided under PCT Articles 22(1) or 39(1). If the search fee is not paid in due time the application shall be deemed to be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT ISR generally substitutes for the EP search; however, Admin Council may require or dispense with a supplementary EP search and may reduce the fee. Non-payment of the required search fee causes deemed withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council powers regarding supplementary search and fees (Article 157(3)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council may decide under what conditions and to what extent the supplementary European search report is to be dispensed with and the search fee is to be reduced, and may at any time rescind such decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants the Administrative Council discretion to set or change policy on supplementary searches and fee reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of international application in place of European publication (Article 158)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication under PCT Article 21 of an international application for which the EPO is a designated Office shall, subject to paragraph 3, take the place of the publication of a European patent application and shall be mentioned in the European Patent Bulletin. Such an application shall not be considered as comprised in the state of the art in accordance with Article 54(3) if the conditions laid down in paragraph 2 are not fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT publication can substitute for EP publication, but state-of-the-art effect under Article 54(3) depends on fulfillment of supply/payment/language conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of international application to EPO and national fee payment for PCT publication effects (Article 158(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application shall be supplied to the EPO in one of its official languages. The applicant shall pay to the EPO the national fee provided for in PCT Article 22(1) or 39(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To secure the benefits of PCT publication for EP purpose (including being treated as published in EP Bulletin and possible provisional protection), the applicant must supply the application in an EPO official language and pay the required national fee to the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO publication where international publication is in non-official language (Article 158(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application is published in a language other than one of the official languages of the EPO, that Office shall publish the international application supplied as specified in paragraph 2. Subject to Article 67(3), provisional protection shall be effective from the date of that publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where WIPO publishes in a non-official language, the EPO's own publication (based on the supplied official-language translation and payment) is the operative event for EP bulletin mention and provisional protection timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional Administrative Council and initial appointments (Article 159)
rubrics_metrics.description: States referred to in Article 169(1) shall appoint their representatives to the Administrative Council; the Council shall meet no later than two months after entry into force, particularly to appoint the President of the EPO. The term of the first Chairman shall be four years; terms of two elected members of first Board shall be five and four years respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets transitional timelines and terms for initial Administrative Council and Board appointments after entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and contracting of employees during transitional period (Article 160)
rubrics_metrics.description: Until Service Regulations and conditions of employment adopted, the Administrative Council and President shall recruit necessary employees and conclude short-term contracts; the Administrative Council may lay down general recruitment principles. During a transitional period the Admin Council, after consulting the President, may appoint technically or legally qualified members of national courts and authorities to the Boards of Appeal who may continue national duties; they may be appointed for terms less than five years (not less than one year) and may be reappointed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides temporary employment/appointment rules until permanent service regulations are in place, including recruiting and allowing national judges/officials to serve on appeal bodies for limited terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive expansion and possible restriction of EPO processing (Article 162)
rubrics_metrics.description: European patent applications may be filed with the EPO from the date fixed by the Administrative Council. The Administrative Council may decide that processing may be restricted (e.g., in certain areas of technology), but examination shall in any event be made as to whether EP applications can be accorded a date of filing. If restricted and an application cannot be further processed, the EPO shall communicate this to the applicant and point out that he may make a request for conversion; the EP application shall be deemed withdrawn on receipt of such communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admin Council may phase in EPO activity and restrict processing in specific technologies, but must still establish filing dates; applicants are to be informed and offered conversion options if processing is restricted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for entry as professional representative during transitional period (Article 163(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: During a transitional period any natural person who fulfils: (a) must be a national of a Contracting State; (b) must have his place of business or employment within the territory of one of the Contracting States; (c) must be entitled to represent persons in patent matters before the central industrial property office of the State in which he has his place of business or employment. Entry upon request must be accompanied by a certificate from that central office confirming these conditions. If entitlement is not conditional on special professional qualifications, persons must have habitually acted in patent matters for at least five years unless professional qualification is officially recognised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives substantive eligibility criteria and documentary proof required to be listed as a professional representative during the transitional period, including a five-year habitual practice alternative where no formal qualification is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions for professional representative requirements (Article 163(4)-(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The President of the EPO may grant exemption from the requirement of paragraph 3 first sentence if the applicant furnishes proof that he has acquired the requisite qualification in another way, and may grant exemption from the nationality requirement in special circumstances. The President shall grant exemption from the nationality requirement if on 5 October 1973 the applicant fulfilled the place-of-business and entitlement requirements. Persons in States acceding less than one year before expiry of transitional period may be entered on the list under similar conditions for one year from the date of accession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presidential discretion permits case-by-case exemptions to enable competent representatives to be entered despite formal shortfalls during transitional phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of representatives entered during transitional period (Article 163(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: After expiry of the transitional period, any person whose name was entered on the list during that period shall remain thereon or, on request, be restored thereto, provided that he then fulfils the place-of-business requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional entrants can remain on the professional representative list post-transition provided they meet ongoing residence/business-location criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing Regulations and Protocols integral; Convention prevails in conflict (Article 164)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Implementing Regulations, Protocol on Recognition, Protocol on Privileges and Immunities, Protocol on Centralisation and Protocol on the Interpretation of Article 69 shall be integral parts of this Convention. In case of conflict between the Convention and the Implementing Regulations, the provisions of the Convention shall prevail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes hierarchy: Convention is supreme over Implementing Regulations in case of conflict; identifies which instruments are integral parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, ratification and accession formalities (Articles 165-166)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convention open for signature until 5 April 1974 by specified States. Convention subject to ratification; instruments to be deposited with the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany. Open to accession by listed categories of States; instruments of accession to be deposited with the German Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies procedural formalities and depositary for signatures, ratifications and accessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible reservations (Article 167)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State may, at signature or ratification/accession, make only the reservations specified: (a) that European patents conferring protection on chemical, pharmaceutical or food products as such shall be ineffective or revocable; (b) that EPs conferring protection on certain agricultural/horticultural processes shall be ineffective or revocable; (c) EPs may have a term shorter than twenty years; (d) not bound by the Protocol on Recognition. Reservations have effect for not more than ten years, subject to possible five-year extension by Admin Council under conditions; must be withdrawn when circumstances permit; effect continues for term of patents filed during reservation period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may make narrow substantive reservations affecting patentable subject-matter or term, subject to time limits and possible administrative extensions; effects on patents filed during reservation period persist for patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Territorial field of application (Article 168)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State may declare in its instrument of ratification or accession, or later by notification, that the Convention shall be applicable to one or more of the territories for whose external relations it is responsible. European patents granted for that State shall also have effect in those territories. Declarations take effect according to timing rules; States may later declare cessation of applicability with one-year effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables territorial extension (or cessation) of the Convention's application for overseas territories or dependencies, with specified effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force conditions (Article 169)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention shall enter into force three months after deposit of the last instrument of ratification or accession by six States on whose territory the total number of patent applications filed in 1970 amounted to at least 180,000 for all the said States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry into force requires both a quorum of States and an aggregate patent-filing activity threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial contribution by later ratifying/accessing States (Article 170)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State which ratifies or accedes after entry into force shall pay an initial contribution (non-refundable) equal to 5% of an amount calculated by applying the percentage obtained for the State to the sum of special financial contributions due from the other Contracting States in respect of prior accounting periods, with substitutive rules if no special contributions were required in the immediate preceding accounting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines financial entry obligations for late joiners, with calculation tied to contribution scales and prior accounting periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and revision (Articles 171-172)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention is of unlimited duration. It may be revised by a Conference convened by the Administrative Council; the Conference must have at least three quarters of Contracting States represented and adopt revisions by three-quarters majority of those represented and voting. Revised text enters into force when ratified/acceded to by number specified by the Conference; states not ratifying cease to be parties when revision enters into force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets durable status but provides structured revision mechanism with supermajority voting and consequences for non-ratifying States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution between Contracting States (Article 173)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute concerning interpretation or application not settled by negotiation shall be submitted, at the request of one State, to the Administrative Council which shall endeavour to bring about agreement. If not reached within six months, any State concerned may submit the dispute to the International Court of Justice for a binding decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates administrative dispute-handling first, with escalation to ICJ after six months if unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure (Article 174)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State may at any time denounce the Convention by notifying the Government of the Federal Republic of Germany. Denunciation takes effect one year after receipt of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple unilateral exit mechanism with one-year delayed effect and depositary notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of acquired rights on cessation (Article 175)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a State ceases to be a party pursuant to Article 172(4) or Article 174, rights already acquired pursuant to the Convention shall not be impaired. A European patent application pending when a designated State ceases to be party shall be processed by the EPO, in so far as that State is concerned, as if the Convention in force thereafter were applicable to that State. Applies likewise to pending oppositions or opposition periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects existing rights and pending procedures in relation to States that cease participation, ensuring continuity for affected applications/patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial rights and obligations of former Contracting State (Article 176)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State ceasing to be party shall have special financial contributions refunded only at the times/conditions applied to other States. The State shall, even after ceasing to be party, continue to pay its proportion of renewal fees in respect of European patents remaining in force in that State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies continuing financial responsibilities and refund limitations for states that withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages and authenticity of Convention texts (Article 177)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Convention is drawn up in English, French and German, the three texts being equally authentic. Texts in other official languages of Contracting States, if approved by the Administrative Council, shall be considered official texts. In event of conflict, the three texts in English, French and German are authentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declares multilingual authenticity and designates the authoritative language set for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and notifications by depositary (Article 178)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government of the Federal Republic of Germany shall draw up certified true copies and transmit them to the Governments of signatory or acceding States, and shall notify Governments of any signature, deposit of instruments, reservations/withdrawals, declarations under territorial application, date of entry into force, and denunciations; and shall register the Convention with the UN Secretariat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigns depositary duties and required notifications to the German Government, including UN registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing Regulations — Languages of the EPO proceedings (Rules 1–7, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing Regulations contain provisions on derogations from language provisions concerning written and oral proceedings; change of language of proceedings; language of a European divisional application; certification of translations; time limits and reduction of fees; legal authenticity of translations of the European patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Implementing Regulations set detailed operational rules on language issues, translation certification, fee reductions tied to language/time limits, and when derogations or language changes are permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organisation of the European Patent Office (Rules 8–12, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules cover patent classification; allocation of duties to departments of first instance; allocation of duties and designation of members of departments of second instance; Rules of Procedure of departments of second instance; administrative structure of the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements organisational and procedural allocation of responsibilities inside EPO for examination and appeal functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure where applicant or proprietor not entitled (Rules 13–15, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules address suspension of proceedings; limitations of the option to withdraw the EP application; and filing of a new EP application by the person entitled to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanisms to suspend processing, restrict withdrawal options, and permit the entitled party to file and regularise rights when entitlement issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of the inventor — designation, publication, rectification (Rules 17–19, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules specify designation of the inventor, publication of the mention of the inventor, and rectification of the designation of an inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets administrative requirements and remedies relating to the inventor's designation and public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registering transfers, licences and other rights (Rules 20–22, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for registering a transfer; registering of licences and other rights; and special indications for registration of a licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the formalities and data required to record changes in ownership and licences in the EPO register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of exhibition (Rule 23, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule provides for issuance of a certificate of exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative proof of exhibition events relevant to priority or novelty considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of the European patent application and divisional applications (Rules 24–25, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapters include general provisions for filing and specific provisions for European divisional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing Regulations set formal filing requirements and special rules governing divisional filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions governing the application (Rules 26–36, Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter II of Part III contains multiple rules (26–36) governing detailed provisions of the application (contents not fully reproduced in this chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates comprehensive procedural and substantive requirements for application content, formalities, amendments, and related matters as set out in the Implementing Regulations.
